title: Benchmark Report (Latency/$) — PDF Layout & Production Notes (v1)
body:
Purpose
- This doc captures production/layout decisions for the downloadable PDF version of the public benchmark report. It’s meant to be a single source of truth for figure placement, caption + footnote language, disclaimers, and export settings.
- Audience: marketing design + content + PMM + legal (final approve) + Applied ML (methodology accuracy).

Doc ownership + workflow
- Owner: Alicia (layout/visual system). Content owner: Ethan. PMM/launch: Soojin.
- Legal review gate: Michael + Sofia must approve: (a) headline/subhead claims, (b) any use of “best / fastest / lowest cost”, (c) competitor-context language, (d) footnote/disclaimer block.
- Applied ML review gate: Jonas + Claire approve: charts match dataset version + metric definition and that captions don’t overgeneralize.

PDF spec (target)
- Format: US Letter (8.5 x 11) portrait.
- Page target: 18–24 pages (current layout plan below is 20 pages).
- Color: RGB (screen-first). No CMYK conversion unless PR requests it.
- Typography: Redwood brand type system (use site-approved fonts; avoid fonts that don’t embed cleanly).
- Accessibility: ensure selectable text (no “flattened” text layers), tagged PDF if export supports it. Provide alt-text for charts where possible (at minimum, descriptive figure captions + appendix table).

Export settings (for final deliverable)
- Export: PDF (Print) but optimized for web distribution.
- Compatibility: Acrobat 10+.
- Embed fonts: on.
- Image handling: downsample to 150–200 ppi for photos; charts/line art preserve vector where possible.
- Compression: medium (keep under ~12–15 MB). If > 15 MB, reduce any background textures and downsample screenshots.
- Links: make URL and email links clickable (landing page, interactive table, methodology page).
- Bleed/crop: no bleed required (web download). Keep safe margins (see grid).
- File naming: redwood-inference-latency-per-dollar-benchmark-report-2025-07-v1.pdf (date stamp may change at publish; use v1.1 if content updates post-legal).
- Final checks before upload:
  - Spell check + link check.
  - Chart labels legible at 100% zoom on laptop.
  - Footnotes consistent across pages.
  - No internal-only terms: “redwood internal”, run IDs, cluster names, region capacity notes.

Grid + margins
- Margins: 0.75" top/bottom, 0.85" left/right (slightly wider to improve printability).
- 12-column grid with 0.2" gutters.
- Body text width: 8 columns (centered) for narrative pages; allow full-width for large charts.
- Figure numbering style: Figure 1, Figure 2… (consistent). Table numbering: Table 1…

High-level page plan (v1)
Page 1 — Cover
- Title: “Latency per Dollar: Production Inference Benchmarks (2025)”
- Subtitle: “A reproducible look at latency, throughput, and cost efficiency across models and regions.”
- Visual: subtle hero chart motif (abstracted) + Redwood logo.
- Required cover disclaimer (small type): “Benchmarks reflect the stated workload configuration and run window. See Methodology and Limitations.”

Page 2 — Executive summary
- 3–5 bullets (no numeric superlatives unless fully substantiated in the PDF itself).
- CTA box (right rail): “Explore interactive results” + short URL + QR code.
- Include “What this is / What this isn’t” callout:
  - Is: production-oriented workload mix; includes p50/p95; regions; cost normalization.
  - Isn’t: a universal ranking; not a guarantee for every prompt/app.

Page 3 — Why latency/$ (metric definition)
- One simple diagram: request lifecycle (prefill vs decode) + where costs accrue.
- Define metrics used throughout:
  - Latency/$ (primary)
  - p50, p95 latency
  - Throughput (tokens/sec)
  - $/1M tokens (or equivalent cost normalization)
- Footnote anchor: “Latency/$ is computed using published pricing at time of test + measured latency under stated concurrency; details in Methodology.”

Page 4 — Methodology overview (1-page summary)
- Keep this page “skimmable”:
  - Workload mix (prefill/decode)
  - Concurrency levels
  - Prompt set summary (v3 production mix)
  - Regions tested
  - Warmup + stability gates
- Visual: 4-up icon grid.
- Bottom: “Full methodology” link + QR.

Pages 5–6 — Methodology detail (2 pages)
- Page 5: Workloads + prompt set
  - Include small table: input tokens range, output tokens range, distribution notes.
  - Callout: “We publish prompt set characteristics; we do not publish raw prompts if licensing restricts.”
- Page 6: Measurement + aggregation
  - Include chart: example distribution; show why p95 matters.
  - Include “Stability gates” blurb: rerun threshold when p95 variance exceeds set threshold.
  - Explicitly state caching/batching policy as used in the published runs (must match final methodology lock).

Page 7 — Results overview (hero chart)
- Figure 1: “Latency/$ by model (overall)”
  - Full-width bar chart or dot plot.
  - Sort: best to worst (or group by model family), but avoid implying “winner” language in headline.
- Caption must include:
  - run window
  - regions included in the aggregate
  - concurrency/workload definition
- Footnote: “Overall results are aggregated across regions using stated weighting; see Appendix for per-region tables.”

Page 8 — Regional consistency
- Figure 2: heatmap “Latency/$ by model x region”
- Visual notes:
  - Use colorblind-safe palette.
  - Put actual values in cells for PDF readability (don’t rely on hover like web).
- Add “How to read this heatmap” 2–3 bullets.

Page 9 — Tail latency (p95)
- Figure 3: p95 latency by model (and region band if space).
- Add callout: “If your app is user-facing or streaming, p95 is often more predictive than p50.”
- Footnote: explain whether streaming endpoints measured time-to-first-token vs full completion (must be consistent with what we measured; avoid mixing).

Page 10 — Cost metric ($/1M tokens)
- Figure 4: $/1M tokens by model
- Add small annotation: “Cost estimates incorporate measured throughput under the same workload; pricing as of <date>.”

Page 11 — Throughput (tokens/sec) with caveat
- Figure 5: tokens/sec
- Caption must state: “Tokens/sec alone can mislead; compare alongside latency distribution and cost normalization.”

Page 12 — Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (positioning, non-competitive)
- 3-column table:
  - Hosted API: fastest start, elastic
  - Dedicated: predictable throughput, isolation
  - Private: VPC/on-prem, compliance
- CTA box: “Talk to us about Dedicated sizing” + link.
- Important: do not imply benchmark results automatically transfer to Private/on-prem without stating: “Private results depend on customer hardware/network.”

Page 13 — How to reproduce (high level)
- Step list (no internal commands; keep public-safe):
  1) Use the published model version
  2) Use provided prompt distribution / token sizes
  3) Run with stated concurrency
  4) Use same regions (or document differences)
  5) Report p50/p95 and latency/$
- Include link to “reproducibility artifacts” page (or GitHub repo if public).

Pages 14–15 — Notable insights + use cases
- Page 14: 3 insights (short)
  - Example structure: “Observation → Why it matters → Who should care”
- Page 15: 3 workloads (customer archetypes) with metric priority
  - Support automation: p95 + streaming stability
  - RAG: prefill sensitivity
  - Agentic tools: consistency + throughput
- Avoid naming customers unless approvals are complete.

Page 16 — Limitations (must-have)
- Bullet list of limitations (plain language):
  - Results depend on prompt/token distribution
  - Regional latency depends on client proximity and network
  - Provider capacity variability; we mitigated via repeat runs but variance exists
  - Software and kernel selection changes can shift results; we freeze versions for the report
  - Competitor context (if included) is directional and based on publicly available info / controlled comparisons as stated

Page 17 — Appendix A: tested configurations
- Table 1: Models + versions (and any quantization profile if applicable)
- Table 2: Regions tested
- Table 3: Concurrency + request patterns
- Small type is fine but must be readable.

Page 18 — Appendix B: metric definitions
- Formal definitions in one place (reduces repetition in captions).
- Include definitions for:
  - prefill latency vs decode latency (if we break out)
  - p50/p95
  - retries/timeouts handling (exclusions)
  - how failures are treated

Page 19 — Appendix C: disclosure + data retention statement (public-facing)
- Short disclosure paragraph:
  - “We retain underlying run manifests and raw logs to substantiate public claims; sensitive identifiers are redacted from public artifacts.”
- Provide contact: benchmarks@redwoodinference.com (confirm before publish).

Page 20 — Closing page
- CTA: “Try Redwood API” + “Talk to Sales”
- Links: docs, interactive benchmark page, methodology page.
- Optional: small “Changelog” line if we expect refreshes.

Figures: placement + caption drafting notes
- General caption style:
  - 1st sentence: what the figure shows.
  - 2nd sentence: workload + concurrency + region scope.
  - Final clause: run window + dataset version.
- Each figure caption must include dataset version string (example format): “Dataset: latency-per-dollar-v1.0 (run window: 2025-06-20 to 2025-06-27).”
- Do not include internal run IDs or manifest filenames in the PDF body.

Required footnotes/disclaimers (copy blocks)
- Standard footnote block (use consistent text, can be abbreviated in some pages with “See Limitations”):
  - “Benchmark results reflect Redwood Inference measurements under the stated methodology (workload mix, concurrency, regions, software versions) during the stated run window. Results may vary by prompt distribution, networking conditions, and service configuration. This report is not a performance guarantee.”
- Comparative claims disclaimer (ONLY if we include any competitor references anywhere in the PDF):
  - “Any third-party comparisons are provided for context and are based on publicly available information and/or controlled tests described in the Methodology. Third-party offerings and pricing may change.”
- Pricing/time disclaimer (needed on any page that shows cost or latency/$):
  - “Cost normalization uses pricing as of <DATE> and measured performance under test conditions; see Methodology for details.”
- Data residency disclaimer (if we mention EU residency or ‘in-region’):
  - “Data residency and compliance depend on the selected deployment mode and region configuration. Contact Redwood for details.”

Callouts to keep consistent with web experience
- Label “latency/$” exactly as “Latency per dollar (latency/$)” on first mention; later can shorten.
- Regions must match the interactive table naming convention (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west, apac-*). Confirm final names with Felix/Wei.
- Use the same model naming as the catalog (no shorthand that mismatches the table).

Design details (practical)
- Heatmaps: include numbers in cells; avoid tiny legend-only interpretation.
- P95 charts: emphasize that p95 relates to tail; keep annotation simple.
- Screenshots of the interactive page: keep at 2x resolution; avoid tiny UI text.
- QR codes: test with phone camera from printed page at 100% scale; add short URL underneath.

Open items (need confirmation before final)
- Final dataset version string + run window.
- Final list of “supported vs experimental” regions/models for publication (Product thread indicated some regions may be excluded).
- Whether streaming metrics are included; if yes, define the exact metric (TTFT vs time-to-completion) and keep consistent across figures.
- Confirm final legal-approved wording for:
  - “production inference economics”
  - “reproducible”
  - “latency/$” label alternatives (if any)

Change log
- 2025-06-11: initial page plan + export notes.
- 2025-06-24: added legal-required Limitations page and comparative disclaimer block (per legal claims review).
- 2025-07-07: updated appendix plan to include metric definitions + disclosure page; tightened caption requirements to include dataset version on every figure.
